description: Behavioural obligations for the v0.5 addressed submit path — destination validation, the honest ack, the misroute detector, and idempotent-replay Caller binding. Several are schema-inexpressible by construction: the submit-ack schema cannot know whether the SUBMIT carried `to`, so 'every addressed ack carries `destination`' is checkable only behaviourally for the `open` statuses (the closed schema enforces it for the addressed-only statuses queued/bounced; `open`/`delivered` are shared with the unaddressed path).
obligation: SUBMIT-TIME DESTINATION VALIDATION (§4): (1) The Hub MUST validate `to` at accept time, within the submitter's account: unknown agent.id -> 422 unknown_destination; unknown session -> 422; TERMINAL session -> 410 destination_gone; the same validation applies retroactively to the §13 directive `to`. Accepting an unroutable destination and silently dead-lettering is non-conformant. (2) Cross-account addressing MUST be rejected identically to unknown (422) — no existence oracle. (3) An allowlist-blocked submit (`inter_agent.sender_allowlists`, §8.0/§13.5) MUST collapse to the same 422 unknown_destination — the policy must not become a sender-visible probe of who may reach whom. (4) When the submitting agent lacks session/presence visibility for the destination (§16.4 policy), the terminal-vs-unknown split MUST collapse to 422 for that sender, and the ack snapshot MUST be exactly {"state": "unknown"} with no last_seen — the submit path must not become a session-state or presence oracle the visibility policy denies. (5) Sender-side symmetry: an addressed (or agent.session-bearing) submit from a principal whose own agent.id contains `#` -> 422 invalid_field (the Hub could not attest a representable `from`). (6) The leg is account-opt-in: a Hub MUST NOT accept `to`-addressed submits for an account that has not enabled `inter_agent` (default false). HONEST ACK (§8.1/§5.1): (7) An addressed notify is acked `status: "queued"` — never `delivered` at accept time (it may still bounce or expire unseen; its lifecycle IS the §14.2 track); an addressed ask/task is acked `open` exactly as unaddressed. (8) EVERY addressed ack, of any verb — including the `open` ones the closed schema cannot discriminate — MUST carry the `destination` reachability snapshot (state per the §15.1 session-bearing derivation, gated by §16.4 policy per (4)). MISROUTE DETECTOR (§8.1): (9) Sender-side MUST: an addressed-submit ack WITHOUT `destination` is a pre-0.5 misroute (the envelope landed in a human inbox via the §10 unknown-field robustness rule) — a conformant 0.5 sender surfaces the failure to its caller and SHOULD cancel a misrouted ask via §8.4; §8.0 feature-detection before first use remains required (the ack check closes the rolling-deploy TOCTOU gap). IDEMPOTENT REPLAY (§8.1): (10) Dedup scope is (agent.id, idempotency_key), run-independent, with `agent.session` and `agent.run_id` EXCLUDED from the identical-payload comparison: a crashed-and-restarted agent replaying the same key from a NEW session/run MUST receive the original ack — original `id`, current status of the verb's OWNING track (§7 resolution for ask/task, incl. a bounce reading cancelled/dismissed by system:undeliverable; the delivery track for an addressed notify) — and the ORIGINAL submit's session remains the bound Caller for Response routing (first submit wins, §6). A same-key replay with a differing payload (beyond the excluded fields) -> 409.
